name: Hail-Crag
description: Hail-Crag is a battered rocky world whose surface tells the story of billions of years of cosmic bombardment. Impact craters overlap in dense layers, the newer ones sharp-rimmed and deep, the ancient ones softened into shallow bowls by the slow work of thermal cycling. Jagged mountain ranges thrust upward at the boundaries of tectonic plates that locked in place eons ago, their peaks dusted with frost that sublimes in the thin air during the long days.

The temperature swings are extreme, scorching under the unfiltered sun and plummeting far below freezing during the long nights. The thin atmosphere offers no protection from solar radiation, and the surface is bathed in harsh ultraviolet that bleaches exposed rock to a chalky white. Wind barely exists here, and in the silence, the only movement is the slow creep of thermal fractures spreading through the stone.

A scattered debris field of escape pods marks the site of some forgotten emergency, their hulls partially buried in regolith and pitted by micrometeorite impacts. The pods appear to date from several decades ago, and their emergency transponders have long since exhausted their power supplies. The occupants, if they survived landing, left no trace that surface surveys have been able to locate.

Hail-Crag's mineral deposits are modest but accessible, and the planet's location along a minor trade route gives it strategic value as a potential waystation. The escape pod mystery draws occasional salvage crews who hope to find valuable cargo or identifiable remains that might carry a reward. The planet itself is indifferent to these visitors, continuing its slow accumulation of impact scars and its patient, grinding transformation of mountains into dust.
